name: FirstUK Bank Production Runbook
description: Internal operational reference document for FirstUK Bank technology and operations teams, providing production procedures and runbook guidance. Effective from 2026-01-15 with scheduled review on 2027-01-15. Intended audience includes Operations Team, On-Call Engineers, and Support Staff.
context: Audience | Operations Team, On-Call Engineers, Support Staff

name: Infrastructure Manager
description: Owner and responsible party for the Production Runbook document within FirstUK Bank. Acts as the primary point of accountability for operational procedures and runbook maintenance.

name: Technology/Operations Department
description: Department responsible for maintaining and executing the Production Runbook at FirstUK Bank. Oversees infrastructure, systems, and operational procedures.

name: Operations Team
description: Primary audience for the Production Runbook, responsible for executing operational procedures and managing production systems at FirstUK Bank.
context: Audience | Operations Team, On-Call Engineers, Support Staff

name: On-Call Engineers
description: On-call technical staff at FirstUK Bank who use the Production Runbook to respond to operational incidents and system issues.
context: Audience | Operations Team, On-Call Engineers, Support Staff

name: Support Staff
description: Support personnel at FirstUK Bank who reference the Production Runbook for operational guidance and procedures.
context: Audience | Operations Team, On-Call Engineers, Support Staff

name: FirstUK Bank
description: The banking institution for which this operational reference document provides procedures for day-to-day operations, system health checks, incident response, and disaster recovery across all production systems.
context: Provide step-by-step procedures for day-to-day operations, system health checks, incident response, and disaster recovery for all FirstUK Bank production systems.

name: Day-to-Day Operations Procedure
description: Step-by-step procedures for routine day-to-day operational activities across FirstUK Bank production systems, forming part of the standard operational reference documentation.
context: Provide step-by-step procedures for day-to-day operations, system health checks, incident response, and disaster recovery for all FirstUK Bank production systems.

name: System Health Check
description: Systematic procedures for monitoring and verifying the health and status of FirstUK Bank production systems as part of routine operational oversight.
context: Provide step-by-step procedures for day-to-day operations, system health checks, incident response, and disaster recovery for all FirstUK Bank production systems.

name: Incident Response Procedure
description: Step-by-step procedures for responding to and managing incidents affecting FirstUK Bank production systems, documented as part of the operational reference framework.
context: Provide step-by-step procedures for day-to-day operations, system health checks, incident response, and disaster recovery for all FirstUK Bank production systems.

name: Disaster Recovery Procedure
description: Step-by-step procedures for disaster recovery and restoration of FirstUK Bank production systems following major incidents or system failures.
context: Provide step-by-step procedures for day-to-day operations, system health checks, incident response, and disaster recovery for all FirstUK Bank production systems.

name: Account Management System
description: Core banking system component monitored as part of daily pre-business operations. Status must be verified as 'Green' during the 07:00 AM operational checklist to ensure system readiness before business hours.

name: Internet Banking Platform
description: Customer-facing internet banking platform monitored during pre-business operations. Status verification is part of the mandatory 15-minute operational checklist.

name: Mobile Banking Application
description: Mobile banking application monitored as part of daily pre-business system health checks. Status must be 'Green' before business operations commence.

name: Payment Processing System
description: Payment processing infrastructure monitored during pre-business operations checklist. Status verification ensures payment systems are operational before business hours.

name: Dashboard Status Check
description: Daily pre-business operational detection step requiring opening the ops dashboard and verifying status of four critical systems (AMS, IBP, MBA, PPS). All statuses must show 'Green' to proceed with business operations.
context: Check Dashboard — Open ops dashboard at https://dashboard.firstuk.bank

name: Overnight Alert Review
description: Daily pre-business detection action to review alert queue for any issues reported during overnight hours (00:00–07:00). Critical alerts must be addressed immediately using kubectl command to query production events.
context: Review Alerts Overnight — Check alert queue for any issues reported 00:00–07:00
Command: `kubectl get events -n production | grep -i warning`
Action: Address any critical alerts immediately

name: Database Backup Verification
description: Daily pre-business operational check to verify that database backups have completed successfully. Most recent backup must be within the last 24 hours using AWS S3 verification.
context: Verify Database Backups — Check last backup completed
Expected: Most recent backup within last 24 hours

name: Payment Systems Connection Verification
description: Daily pre-business operational check to verify that BACS and FPS payment system connections are active and operational. Health check API call must return 'ok' status.
context: Check Payment Systems — Verify BACS/FPS connections active

name: Incident Response Escalation
description: Escalation action triggered when any critical issue is found during pre-business operations checklist. Directs operations team to proceed to Step 6 (Incident Response) procedures.
context: Issue Found? → Go to Step 6 (Incident Response)

name: Daily Operations Checklist
description: Operational reference guide for pre-business hours procedures, detailing the mandatory 15-minute checklist that must be completed at 07:00 AM before business operations commence. Includes dashboard verification, alert review, backup confirmation, and payment system checks.
context: Issue Found? → Go to Step 6 (Incident Response)

name: API Gateway Health Check
description: Hourly monitoring procedure during business hours to verify Kong API gateway status and response times. Executed via command-line health check with expected threshold of all services responding under 100ms.
context: API Gateway Health — Monitor Kong gateway

name: Database Connection Pool Check
description: Hourly monitoring procedure to verify PostgreSQL database connection pool utilization during business hours. Checks that active connections remain below 80% of maximum capacity (200 of 250 connections).
context: Database Connection Pool — Check PostgreSQL connections
Command: `psql -U postgres -c "SELECT datname, count(*) FROM pg_stat_activity GROUP BY datname;"`

name: Transaction Processing Rate Monitoring
description: Hourly monitoring procedure to track transaction processing throughput during business hours. Monitors transaction log for successful completions with expected rate of 2–5 transactions per minute.

name: Incident Response Escalation
description: Escalation procedure triggered when any of the hourly health checks during business hours (09:00–17:00) detect a threshold breach or service anomaly.
context: Issue Found? → Go to Step 6 (Incident Response)

name: Payment Settlement Confirmation
description: End-of-business verification that all FPS and BACS payments have been settled by the expected cutoff time of 17:30. This is a daily operational checkpoint performed at 17:00 PM as part of the end-of-business checklist.
context: Payment Settlement Confirmation — Verify daily settlement completed
Expected: All FPS/BACS payments settled by 17:30

name: Reconciliation Report
description: Nightly reconciliation process executed via automated script to verify all transactions have been reconciled. The process is triggered by running the reconciliation.py script and expects a PASS result confirming full reconciliation.

name: Backup Initiation
description: Nightly backup procedure that synchronizes data from the local backup directory to AWS S3 storage using AES256 encryption. Executed as part of the end-of-business checklist to ensure data protection and disaster recovery capability.

name: Data Warehouse Load
description: Nightly data warehouse load process triggered via Spark job submission that inserts reconciled transaction data into the data warehouse. Executed as the final step of the end-of-business checklist.
context: Data Warehouse Load — Trigger nightly DW load

name: System Startup
description: Emergency procedure executed following complete system outage or scheduled maintenance restart. This action represents the controlled restoration of banking systems to operational status after a total service interruption.
context: After complete outage or scheduled maintenance restart

name: Database Startup Phase
description: Initial startup phase for PostgreSQL database infrastructure, including service start, version verification, replication slot validation, and backup confirmation. This phase must complete successfully before proceeding to core application startup.
context: Verify replication psql -U postgres -c "SELECT slot_name, restart_lsn FROM pg_replication_slots;"

name: Core Applications Startup Phase
description: Deployment and health verification of three critical banking services: Account Management System (AMS), Payment Processing System (PPS), and Fraud Detection Engine (FDE). Each service is deployed via Kubernetes with a 5-minute rollout timeout and verified to reach Running state.

name: Customer-Facing Services Startup Phase
description: Deployment of Internet Banking Platform (IBP) and Mobile Banking Application backend (MBA), followed by cache clearing and endpoint health verification. This phase enables customer access to banking services.
context: Start MBA (Mobile App backend) kubectl apply -f /deployments/mba-deployment.yaml

name: System Verification and Notification Phase
description: Final validation phase including automated smoke test execution, dashboard status confirmation, and team notification via operations channel. All systems must return Green status before startup is considered complete.
context: Run smoke tests bash /tests/smoke_tests.sh Expected: All tests PASS
Verify dashboard Check https://dashboard.firstuk.bank Expected: All systems Green
Notify team Post to #operations-channel: "Systems startup complete"

name: Incident Response Escalation
description: Mandatory escalation procedure triggered if any startup phase fails. Operations must halt progression to subsequent phases and immediately invoke incident response protocols rather than continuing with the startup sequence.
context: If Any Phase Fails: Go to Step 6 (Incident Response) — Do NOT proceed to next phase

name: Operations Team Channel
description: Internal Slack channel used for operational notifications and team coordination. Receives system startup completion notifications and operational status updates.

name: System Shutdown
description: A planned, controlled system shutdown performed during scheduled maintenance windows. This is a routine operational procedure distinct from unplanned outages or emergency shutdowns, used to perform system updates, patches, or infrastructure maintenance.

name: Customer Notification for Maintenance
description: Initial phase of shutdown sequence requiring notification to all customers of planned system maintenance. Includes posting website banner and optional SMS alert to inform customers of the maintenance window timing.

name: Graceful Shutdown Procedure
description: Multi-step controlled shutdown sequence lasting approximately 20 minutes. Involves stopping transaction acceptance, allowing in-flight transactions to complete, halting payment processing, stopping application servers, backing up the database, and stopping the database service.
context: Wait for in-flight transactions to complete

name: Shutdown Completion Notification
description: Final phase of shutdown sequence requiring internal operations team notification that system shutdown has been completed successfully.

name: Operations Team
description: Internal operations team responsible for receiving shutdown completion notification via the #operations channel.

name: Maintenance Window Notification
description: Customer-facing guidance communicating planned system maintenance timing and availability impact. Delivered via website banner and optional SMS alert.
context: Check: Maintenance window during low-traffic time

name: AMS Service Unavailable
description: A system outage affecting the AMS (Account Management Service) API, characterized by 503 service unavailable responses and error display in the IBP interface. The incident may stem from service pod failures, database connectivity issues, or connection pool exhaustion.
context: Check service status kubectl get pod -n production | grep ams
Verify PostgreSQL running: systemctl status postgresql@main
Restart service kubectl rollout restart deployment/ams

name: Service Status Check
description: Initial diagnostic step to verify the operational status of AMS service pods in the production Kubernetes cluster. Executed as the first troubleshooting action when AMS Service Unavailable is reported.
context: kubectl get pod -n production | grep ams

name: Service Log Review
description: Examination of the most recent 50 lines of AMS deployment logs to identify error messages, stack traces, or operational anomalies contributing to the outage.

name: Database Connection Health Check
description: API-based health check to verify connectivity between the AMS service and its PostgreSQL database backend. A successful response indicates the database connection is operational.

name: PostgreSQL Service Verification
description: System-level verification that the PostgreSQL database service is running on the main instance. Executed when database connectivity issues are suspected.
context: Verify PostgreSQL running: systemctl status postgresql@main

name: Database Connection Pool Analysis
description: Query of PostgreSQL system tables to count active database connections for the firstuk_prod database. Identifies connection pool exhaustion as a potential root cause.
context: Verify connection pool: psql -U postgres -c "SELECT count(*) FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE datname='firstuk_prod';"

name: AMS Service Restart
description: Kubernetes-based restart of the AMS deployment to recover from transient failures or resource exhaustion. Includes rollout status monitoring with a 5-minute timeout.

name: Service Recovery Verification
description: API call to the accounts endpoint with bearer token authentication to confirm that the AMS service has recovered and is returning account data successfully.

name: Payment Processing Slow
description: A performance degradation incident affecting Faster Payment Service (FPS) transfers and BACS payments, characterized by transfers taking longer than 15 minutes to process. The incident involves monitoring payment queue length, database I/O wait events, and resource constraints on the payment processing system.
context: FPS transfers taking >15 minutes, BACS delayed
If queue growing Monitor: kubectl logs -f deployment/pps | grep "pending"
If high I/O wait Increase database resources: kubectl set resources deployment/ams --limits=memory=4Gi,cpu=2

name: Check Payment Queue
description: Initial detection step to assess the payment processing queue status by querying the payment processing system API endpoint. This is the first diagnostic action in the Payment Processing Slow incident response procedure.

name: Monitor Payment Queue Logs
description: Conditional investigation step executed when the payment queue is growing, using Kubernetes logs to identify pending payment transactions in the payment processing system deployment.
context: If queue growing Monitor: kubectl logs -f deployment/pps | grep "pending"

name: Check Database I/O Wait Events
description: Diagnostic query executed against the PostgreSQL database to determine if I/O wait events are causing the payment processing bottleneck. Identifies whether database resource constraints are the root cause.
context: Check if database is bottleneck psql -U postgres -c "SELECT count(*) FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE wait_event_type='IO';"

name: Increase Database Resources
description: Containment and recovery action triggered when high I/O wait is detected on the database. Increases memory and CPU limits on the application management system (AMS) deployment to resolve resource constraints.
context: If high I/O wait Increase database resources: kubectl set resources deployment/ams --limits=memory=4Gi,cpu=2

name: Monitor Queue Recovery
description: Post-remediation monitoring step to verify that the payment queue is decreasing and the incident is resolving. Continuously polls the payment processing system API to track recovery progress.
context: Monitor recovery Watch queue decrease: watch 'curl https://api.firstuk.bank/pps/queue-length'

name: Escalate to Database Team
description: Final escalation action executed if the payment queue does not improve after resource increase. Transfers incident ownership to the database team for deeper investigation and remediation.
context: If not improving Escalate to database team (see Step 6)

name: High Fraud Alert Rate
description: A fraud detection system alert condition triggered when the Fraud Detection Engine (FDE) generates an abnormally high volume of alerts, with many flagged as false positives affecting legitimate customer transactions. The baseline threshold is <10 alerts per hour; escalation occurs when alert rate exceeds 3x normal levels.
context: Many legitimate transactions flagged as fraud, customer complaints

name: Fraud Detection Engine Alert Rate Check
description: Initial detection step to measure the current Fraud Detection Engine alert rate and compare against the established baseline of <10 alerts per hour using kubectl logs.

name: Recent Fraud Alert Review
description: Investigation step to examine the most recent 100 fraud alerts from the FDE log, filtering specifically for false positive entries to identify patterns and root causes.

name: DDoS or Attack Detection Check
description: Conditional investigation step triggered when alert rate exceeds 3x normal levels, checking for potential DDoS attacks or coordinated malicious activity in the production environment.
context: Check for DDoS/attack: kubectl get events -n production

name: Fraud Detection Rules Adjustment
description: Containment action to temporarily relax fraud detection rules by editing the fraud_rules.yaml configuration file and restarting the FDE service to reduce false positive rate while investigation continues.

name: Financial Crime Team Notification
description: Mandatory notification step to alert the Financial Crime team when fraud detection rules are temporarily adjusted due to high false positive rates.

name: False Positive Review Meeting
description: Scheduled urgent meeting with the fraud detection and Financial Crime teams to review false positive patterns and determine root causes before restoring normal detection settings.
context: Schedule urgent meeting to review false positives

name: Fraud Detection Rules Restoration
description: Post-incident recovery step to revert fraud detection rules to their normal configuration once the root cause has been identified and resolved.

name: Financial Crime Team
description: Internal team responsible for monitoring and responding to fraud detection system alerts and false positive investigations. Must be notified when fraud detection rules are temporarily modified.

name: Fraud Detection System Failure
description: An operational incident where the Fraud Detection Engine generates an abnormally high volume of false positive alerts, causing legitimate customer transactions to be incorrectly flagged and triggering customer complaints.
context: Many legitimate transactions flagged as fraud, customer complaints

name: Severity Level - Critical
description: Critical severity level triggered when system is completely down. Requires immediate escalation with no delay. This is the highest priority incident classification in the response flowchart.

name: Severity Level - High
description: High severity level triggered by partial system outage affecting some functionality. Requires escalation within 1 hour of detection.

name: Severity Level - Low
description: Low severity level triggered by degraded system performance. Requires escalation within 4 hours of detection.

name: Severity Assessment
description: Initial triage action to classify detected issues into Critical, High, or Low severity categories. Determines the escalation timeline and response urgency.
context: Severity Assessment ├─ Critical (System Down) → IMMEDIATE ESCALATION

name: Investigation
description: Systematic troubleshooting phase to identify the root cause of the detected issue. Branches into either issue identification leading to fix application, or escalation to team if issue cannot be found.
context: Investigate (See Troubleshooting) ├─ Issue Identified → Apply Fix
└─ Issue Not Found → Escalate to Team

name: Fix Implementation
description: Execution of corrective actions following issue identification. Options include rollback of deployment, service restart, or configuration changes with reload.
context: Implement Fix ├─ Rollback? → Roll back deployment
├─ Restart? → Restart service └─ Config Change? → Update and reload

name: Recovery Verification
description: Validation step to confirm that the applied fix has resolved the issue. Pass results in incident closure and documentation; failure triggers escalation to team lead.
context: Verify Recovery ├─ PASS → Close incident, document

name: Incident Documentation
description: Final phase capturing complete incident record including timeline of actions, root cause analysis, and preventive measures. Ensures organizational learning and future prevention.
context: Document Incident - Record in incident log
- Timeline of actions - Root cause analysis - Prevention measures for future

name: Immediate Escalation
description: Mandatory immediate escalation action triggered for Critical severity incidents with no time delay permitted.

name: One-Hour Escalation
description: Escalation action required for High severity incidents within a 1-hour window from detection.

name: Four-Hour Escalation
description: Escalation action required for Low severity incidents within a 4-hour window from detection.

name: System Incident
description: Operational incident involving system unavailability or degradation. Classified by severity (Critical for complete downtime, High for partial outage, Low for degradation) with corresponding response procedures and escalation timelines.
context: Issue Detected ↓ Severity Assessment ├─ Critical (System Down)
├─ High (Partial Outage) → Escalate within 1 hour └─ Low (Degraded)

name: Severity Critical
description: Critical severity level triggered when system is completely down or major data loss occurs. Requires immediate escalation to On-Call Engineer with 24/7 availability.
context: Critical: System completely down or major data loss

name: Severity High
description: High severity level triggered by partial outages affecting customers. Escalates to Technology Manager during business hours.

name: Severity Medium
description: Medium severity level for performance issues or non-critical system failures. Escalates to Database Team.
context: Medium: Performance issue or non-critical system

name: Severity Low
description: Low severity level for minor issues where the system continues to function. Escalates to Infrastructure team.

name: On-Call Engineer
description: Primary escalation contact for critical severity incidents involving complete system outage or major data loss. Available 24/7 for emergency response.
context: Critical: System completely down or major data loss

name: Technology Manager
description: Escalation contact for high severity incidents involving partial customer outages. Reached via email or extension 5000.

name: Database Team
description: Escalation contact for medium severity incidents involving performance issues or non-critical system failures. Reached via extension 5010.
context: Medium: Performance issue or non-critical system

name: Infrastructure Team
description: Escalation contact for low severity incidents involving minor issues where system functionality is maintained. Reached via extension 5020.

name: Monitoring Dashboard Access and Review
description: Customer-facing guidance on accessing the primary monitoring dashboard at https://dashboard.firstuk.bank and understanding key operational metrics. Provides reference for system health visibility and alert thresholds during normal operations.
context: Check Dashboard: Every hour during business hours, every 4 hours overnight

name: Dashboard Monitoring Check
description: Scheduled operational monitoring action requiring dashboard review at defined intervals to detect performance degradation or system anomalies. Executed hourly during business hours and every 4 hours overnight.
context: Check Dashboard: Every hour during business hours, every 4 hours overnight

name: API Response Time Alert Threshold
description: Performance alert triggered when API response time (p95) exceeds 2 seconds, indicating potential system degradation. Normal operating range is below 500ms.

name: Database Connection Alert Threshold
description: Performance alert triggered when database connections exceed 200, indicating potential connection pool exhaustion. Normal operating range is below 100 connections.

name: Error Rate Alert Threshold
description: Performance alert triggered when system error rate exceeds 1%, indicating elevated transaction failures. Normal operating range is below 0.1%.

name: Memory Usage Alert Threshold
description: Performance alert triggered when memory usage exceeds 85%, indicating potential resource constraint. Normal operating range is below 70%.

name: Disk Usage Alert Threshold
description: Performance alert triggered when disk usage exceeds 80%, indicating potential storage constraint. Normal operating range is below 60%.

name: Payment Success Rate Alert Threshold
description: Operational alert triggered when payment success rate falls below 99%, indicating elevated transaction failure rate. Normal operating range is above 99.9%.

name: Fraud Alert Rate Threshold
description: Security alert triggered when fraud detection alert volume exceeds 30 per hour, indicating potential fraud attack or system misconfiguration. Normal operating range is below 10 alerts per hour.

name: Daily Backup Execution
description: Automated daily backup process executed at 23:59 UTC to AWS S3 with encryption and multi-region replication. Part of the bank's disaster recovery and business continuity framework to ensure data protection and recovery capability.

name: Automated Restore Test
description: Weekly automated verification procedure to test the integrity and recoverability of backup data. Ensures that backup systems function correctly and data can be restored in a disaster recovery scenario.

name: Backup Failure
description: Operational incident involving failure, corruption, or unavailability of the daily backup process or backup storage infrastructure. Directly impacts disaster recovery capability and business continuity.

name: Disaster Recovery Incident
description: System or operational failure requiring activation of disaster recovery procedures and restoration from backup. Encompasses scenarios where primary systems are unavailable and recovery from AWS S3 backups is necessary.

name: Contact Infrastructure Team
description: Initial step in the backup restoration process requiring direct engagement with the Infrastructure team to initiate recovery procedures. This action is the first contact point for triggering system restoration from backup.
context: To Restore from Backup: 1. Contact Infrastructure team

name: Provide Target Restore Time
description: Required action to communicate the specific point in time to which systems should be restored. This information is essential for the Infrastructure team to select the appropriate backup point.

name: Restore from Backup Point
description: Core recovery action performed by the Infrastructure team to restore systems and data from the selected backup point. This is the primary restoration step in the recovery procedure.

name: Verify Data Integrity
description: Validation step to confirm that restored data is complete, uncorrupted, and consistent following the backup restoration. This ensures the integrity of the recovered system state.

name: Bring Systems Online
description: Action to activate and make restored systems operational and available to users and stakeholders. This step transitions systems from recovery mode to production status.

name: Notify Stakeholders
description: Final communication step to inform all relevant stakeholders that systems have been restored and are operational. This ensures transparency and confirms recovery completion.

name: Infrastructure Team
description: Internal technical team responsible for executing backup restoration procedures, managing recovery operations, and bringing systems back online. They are the primary contact for initiating and managing the recovery process.

name: Stakeholders
description: Internal and external parties who require notification upon successful system recovery and restoration. They must be informed when systems are brought back online.

name: Scheduled Maintenance Window
description: Recurring maintenance window scheduled for Tuesdays 02:00–04:00 AM UTC to perform database patching, OS updates, application updates, and network maintenance. Advance notice is posted 1 week prior, with minimal customer impact due to off-peak timing.
context: Database patching, OS updates, Application updates, Network maintenance

name: Maintenance Schedule and Customer Impact Notification
description: Customer-facing guidance explaining the scheduled maintenance window timing, the types of activities performed, advance notice provision, and confirmation of minimal customer impact during off-peak hours.

name: 24/7 On-Call Support Email
description: 24/7 on-call support contact via email for incident escalation and emergency notifications. Available continuously for operational incidents and urgent matters.

name: 24/7 On-Call Support Phone
description: 24/7 on-call support contact via phone for incident escalation and emergency notifications. Available continuously for operational incidents and urgent matters.

name: Incident Response Slack Channel
description: 24/7 Slack channel for incident response team communication and real-time escalation notifications. Used for coordinating incident response activities.

name: Business Hours Help Desk
description: Business hours support contact via internal extension for operational and technical inquiries. Available during standard business hours only.

name: Technology Lead
description: Business hours contact for technology-related escalations and technical leadership decisions. Available during standard business hours.
